item.text: The graded tree is unchanged by the audit. Let me record that integrity check and finalize.

This turn closed out the remaining source review and verified audit integrity.

- Reviewed the snapshot/restore surfaces (`api.go` `restoreSnapshot`/`tryRestoreSingleSnapshot`/`Restore`, `snapshot.go`, `file_snapshot.go`) — all match documented upstream behavior; no defect.
- Integrity re-check: the graded tree (`work/`) is still **byte-identical to the captured `source/`** — `diff -rq` shows no differing files (only the scratch dirs I added), and `raft.go` hashes match. All diagnostic edits stayed under `work/diag/`.
- Report updated with this final integrity evidence.

Overall audit result (unchanged, now fully documented in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-11_16-25-33-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md)):

- The supplied implementation is the **unmodified upstream `github.com/hashicorp/raft` `v1.7.3`** — verified byte-for-byte against both the module artifact Go trusts and its signed checksum-database record. There is no injected defect in the graded module.
- **No concrete correctness defect in the consensus implementation was demonstrated.** Six full-package test runs plus a full `-race` run pass.
- **C1 (confirmed, reproduced):** the shipped test helper `cluster.EnsureSamePeers` (`testing.go:691`) samples `rafts[0]`'s configuration once and never refreshes it; with `TestRaft_HasExistingState` (which applies no commands, so `EnsureSame` is vacuous) this becomes a guaranteed 5s spurious failure in ~18% of runs. Re-sampling inside the loop makes it pass 100/100. This is a test-utility bug, not a consensus-correctness bug.
- The nested `fuzzy/`/`raft-compat/` modules are outside the graded package and cannot be built offline (dependency zips absent, read-only cache, unchecked-out submodule).

Nothing is currently blocking; the audit reached a defensible conclusion. If continued, the only remaining marginal work is source-only review of `net_transport.go` and a quick check for other test helpers using the same sample-once pattern.
